arista-mibs.evidence: DELETED: src/backend/collectors/mibs/vendored/ARISTA-SMI-MIB and .../ARISTA-BRIDGE-EXT-MIB. Fetch mechanism: src/backend/collectors/mibs/gen_index.py FETCH_PINS / fetch_pinned_mibs() (https URLs, pinned sha256, bounded body and time, retry with backoff+jitter, atomic write so a mismatch leaves no partial file); cache path gitignored in .gitignore. Documented in vendored/SOURCES.md and collectors/mibs/README.md. Twelve tests in test_gen_index.py cover every fail-closed path. OFFLINE-BUNDLE HONESTY (checked, not assumed): removing them does NOT break offline install and is therefore not redistribution by another name — nothing in scripts/install.py, scripts/make-installer.sh, Dockerfile.backend or any compose file invokes gen_index.py, mibdump or snmptranslate; the backend embeds only the CHECKED-IN index/oididx.json via go:embed; and the bundle ships prebuilt images the customer loads rather than compiles. With no network the measured loss is exactly 8 OIDs under 1.3.6.1.4.1.30065.3.2 (the Arista FDB table and its conformance nodes); the two v1-form MAC-move traps keep their name and above-the-floor severity because they are hand-anchored in gen_index.py's STD_OVERLAY and read no MIB file.
arista-mibs.obligation: none — Correlix no longer redistributes these files in any form
arista-mibs.owner_decision: DECIDED 2026-09-04 (owner) — FETCH at build time, do not redistribute. Both files are deleted from the repository, so they no longer travel in the customer source tarball and there is nothing left to obtain a redistribution position for.
arista-mibs.posture: RESOLVED by removal. The modules are fetched at build time into a gitignored cache under vendored/.fetched/, pinned by URL and sha256 and verified on every use (cache hits included). A missing pin, an unreachable mirror or a checksum mismatch is a hard failure with a named reason; the only non-fatal path is the operator's explicit MIB_FETCH=0 opt-out, which prints a warning naming exactly what it costs.
arista-mibs.rationale: The two modules carried 'Copyright (c) 2008 Arista Networks, Inc. All rights reserved.' with no licence text. The other ~55 vendor MIBs were already resolved at build time from a mirror and vendored nothing; these two were in-tree only because the SMIv1 net-snmp pass needs real files on disk, which is a build mechanics problem rather than a licensing one. Fetching them into a gitignored cache fixes the mechanics without redistributing anything.

balabit/syslog-ng.evidence: scripts/source-mirror.json is the reviewed pin table (URL + sha256 + size + the split-licence facts, and an explicit record that upstream publishes NO checksum, signature or release-asset digest — the sha256 is our own measurement taken 2026-09-04). scripts/make-installer.sh `write_source_offer()` fetches it into <bundle>/source-offer/syslog-ng-4.7.1.tar.gz with a written README stating the GPL-2.0-or-later / LGPL-2.1-or-later terms, verifies the checksum, FAILS THE BUILD on any fetch or integrity failure, and the file is covered by the bundle's SHA256SUMS. `--source-offer-only` is the dry run. .github/workflows/release-bundle.yml asserts the directory, the README, the archive and its SHA256SUMS entry on every release, and uploads source-offer members as release assets. tests/test_source_offer.py proves the layout, the terms text, the checksum gate and the compose-version drift guard offline.
balabit/syslog-ng.obligation: ship the GPL-2.0 + LGPL-2.1 texts and a written offer for syslog-ng's Corresponding Source
balabit/syslog-ng.owner_decision: DECIDED 2026-09-04 (owner) — MIRROR the exact upstream source tarball into every shipped release, discharging GPL-2.0 §3(a) at hand-over rather than relying on §3(b)'s three-year written offer. The written offer remains in the notices, but now points at the in-bundle copy first.
balabit/syslog-ng.posture: Core archive, unmodified upstream container. Receives syslog over the network and writes to Kafka; no Correlix code is linked into it, and it links to none of ours. GPL-2.0-or-later applies to the syslog-ng combination only.
balabit/syslog-ng.rationale: A three-year offer is a promise that has to outlive repository renames, upstream deletions and company changes; a tarball already in the customer's hands does not. syslog-ng 4.7.1 is also the exact release at which the project's founder forked AxoSyslog, so upstream hosting for this tag is more likely than most to move.

busybox.evidence: DISCOVERY: scripts/oci-compliance.py evaluates a CycloneDX SBOM of each FINAL OCI image (Syft — the scanner .github/workflows/publish-images.yml already runs on every pushed digest) instead of the Dockerfiles that produced it, so BusyBox is found without being declared anywhere. Proven on the real netops-frontend image: busybox 1.37.0-r12, GPL-2.0-only, origin inherited-base-layer (every layer holding it belongs to the pinned nginx:1.27-alpine base), together with the busybox-binsh and ssl_client subpackages built from the same origin package. RETENTION: two entries in scripts/source-mirror.json — the upstream release busybox-1.37.0.tar.bz2 (sha256 checked against BusyBox's OWN published .sha256, so this pin is an upstream attestation rather than a self-measurement) and busybox-1.37.0-r12-alpine-aports.tar.gz, Alpine's complete packaging (APKBUILD + 37 distribution patches + busyboxconfig) archived at the exact aports commit the shipped image's own apk database records. make-installer.sh write_source_offer() mirrors both into every bundle's source-offer/ with no code change — BusyBox is not a special path, it is one more entry in the generic pin table. CORRESPONDENCE: `distro-exact`, and that claim is CHECKED, not asserted — the packaging archive's pinned build_ref must equal the aports commit Syft reads out of /lib/apk/db/installed in the image, or the tool downgrades the claim. GATE: scripts/oci-compliance.py fails a release when required source is missing or its checksum is wrong, and never converts a scanner failure into zero findings; docs/compliance/oci-inventory.json feeds the same facts back into this audit and into docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md, so an inherited component can no longer be invisible. Documented in docs/compliance/OCI_SOURCE_COMPLIANCE.md; regression tests in tests/test_oci_compliance.py, including an alpine base image whose child Dockerfile installs no BusyBox at all.
busybox.obligation: complete corresponding source for the BusyBox in every image Correlix distributes, retained by Correlix and verifiable against a recorded checksum
busybox.owner_decision: DECIDED 2026-09-05 (owner, tracker 238) — MIRROR. The rule is general, not BusyBox-specific: IF CORRELIX SHIPS THE BINARY, CORRELIX RETAINS THE SOURCE, however the binary got into the image — directly added, installed by a package manager, pulled as a dependency, copied in, or INHERITED FROM AN UPSTREAM BASE IMAGE. Upstream availability may be recorded as provenance or used as the retrieval source, but it is not by itself compliance. The de-facto posture the audit §5 recorded (relying on the distribution's own source availability) is therefore superseded for every component Correlix distributes.
busybox.posture: BusyBox is GPL-2.0-ONLY (there is no 'or later' option) and rides inside the Alpine layers of nginx:1.27-alpine, which is the base of the netops-frontend and netops-nginx images Correlix builds and distributes. It is named in NO Correlix Dockerfile, which is why the declaration-based audit could not see it: it models image REFERENCES and this is a base LAYER. The final image is now the compliance boundary.

certifi.evidence: MPL-2.0 notice + upstream source pointer ship in docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md and NOTICE, copied to /app/licenses in deployment/docker/Dockerfile.correlation; certifi's own LICENSE remains in its dist-info inside the image
certifi.obligation: licence text + upstream source pointer in the shipped notices
certifi.posture: Installed unmodified into site-packages in netops-correlation. MPL-2.0 file-level copyleft; we modify nothing, so only the notice + source-availability pointer applies.

cisco-mib-extracts.evidence: src/backend/collectors/mibs/vendored/SNMPv2-TC (RFC 2579, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2579.txt) and .../SNMPv2-CONF (RFC 2580, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2580.txt); provenance and the IETF Trust licence pointer are in each file's header and in vendored/SOURCES.md. Verified by a normalised diff against net-snmp's own upstream IETF copies of both modules — zero differing lines. Parse-verified: `snmptranslate -M vendored -m ALL -Tz` output and stderr are byte-identical before and after, and gen_index's net-snmp pass returns the same 232 nodes. Guarded by src/backend/collectors/mibs/test_gen_index.py::test_the_ietf_modules_replaced_the_cisco_extracts, which was negative-checked. The regenerated index/oididx.json is byte-identical to the previous one, so the swap is content-neutral. These two paths now live under the `ietf-rfc-mibs` vendored entry.
cisco-mib-extracts.obligation: IETF Trust Legal Provisions section 4.e — the Simplified BSD terms for RFC Code Components; the notice ships in each file's header and in the generated notices
cisco-mib-extracts.owner_decision: DECIDED 2026-09-04 (owner) — REPLACE SNMPv2-TC and SNMPv2-CONF with the canonical IETF module text. Not 'accept the risk in writing': remove the ambiguity. The current STD 58 documents (RFC 2579 / RFC 2580) were used rather than the obsoleted RFC 1903/1904 the Cisco files were extracted from.
cisco-mib-extracts.posture: RESOLVED by replacement. Both modules are now the verbatim MIB modules of RFC 2579 and RFC 2580 with the RFC's page furniture removed and an IETF Trust provenance header added. Nothing Cisco-copyright remains in the MIB tree.
cisco-mib-extracts.rationale: The Cisco files carried 'Copyright (c) 1994,1996 by cisco Systems, Inc. All rights reserved.' with no grant of any kind, and they shipped inside the customer source tarball. The RFC text is the same normative content, is unambiguously redistributable as an RFC Code Component, and cost about an hour. Keeping an unlicensed file to save that hour was never the better trade.

cloud-vendor-marks.evidence: DELETED: src/frontend/src/assets/cloud/{aws,azure,gcp}.svg (the SPA now draws inline and needs no asset). REPLACED IN PLACE (the files must remain for `go:embed cloudicons/*.svg`, but hold none of the original content): src/backend/internal/rca/cloudicons/{aws,azure,gcp}.svg. NEW original artwork: src/frontend/src/components/CloudGlyph.tsx. Also replaced: the AwsLogo/AzureLogo/GcpLogo marks that were inlined in src/frontend/src/components/ConnectorLogos.tsx and rendered by tabs/admin.tsx and pages/appobs/providers.tsx — found during implementation and in scope, since D5 is 'every embedded provider logo'. Rationale recorded in the rewritten cloudicons/README.md and assets/cloud/README.md. Guarded by src/backend/internal/rca/rca_report_icons_test.go and src/frontend/src/components/CloudGlyph.test.tsx, which assert no provider brand colour or logo path data survives.
cloud-vendor-marks.obligation: none — no provider mark is redistributed any more
cloud-vendor-marks.owner_decision: DECIDED 2026-09-04 (owner) — REPLACE the AWS, Azure and Google Cloud marks with original, non-trademarked Correlix cloud glyphs. Not 'confirm the use is permitted': remove the question.
cloud-vendor-marks.posture: RESOLVED by replacement. Cloud nodes and RCA reports now draw one original Correlix cloud silhouette in four variants (untagged generic, AWS, AZ, GCP) that differ only by a small plain letter tag. No provider path data, brand colour or gradient remains anywhere in the tree.
cloud-vendor-marks.rationale: The marks were carried under a terms-of-use posture rather than a licence, and the AWS asset was the AWS Cloud LOGO rather than an Architecture Icon, which brings AWS's trademark guidelines into play on top of the icon ToU. The terms also lived in asset READMEs, so they did not travel with the go:embed'd binary. Drawing our own glyph removes the trademark question outright, makes the artwork theme-aware (currentColor instead of fixed brand hues), and costs nothing a customer values: the cloud nodes still read as AWS, Azure and GCP because the glyph carries a plain letter tag, which is a nominative textual reference rather than a mark.

connector-marks.evidence: src/frontend/src/assets/connectors/{jira,servicenow}.svg DELETED 2026-09-03 (zero references in the frontend); the `vendored` entry that tracked them is removed, so nothing ships and nothing needs attribution
connector-marks.obligation: none — the files no longer exist in the tree
connector-marks.owner_decision: none needed — deleted (the audit's recommended option)
connector-marks.posture: RESOLVED by deletion. Two unreferenced Atlassian/ServiceNow marks used to sit in the frontend source tree with no terms recorded and ship inside the source tarball. Nothing referenced them, so they were deleted rather than documented.

connector-vendor-marks.evidence: REMOVED: the ServiceNowLogo / JiraLogo / SlackLogo / TwilioLogo / PagerDutyLogo / TeamsLogo components in src/frontend/src/components/ConnectorLogos.tsx (that file now holds only the D5 cloud-glyph wrappers and carries no colour literal at all). REMOVED: the brand tints `.conn-logo.{servicenow,jira,slack,pagerduty,teams,sns}` in src/frontend/src/styles.css, replaced by one token-derived accent wash. NEW: src/frontend/src/components/ConnectorGlyph.tsx — the connector → display name / category / functional glyph registry, plus the new ticket/board/chat/phone/users/webhook/plug glyphs in components/Icon.tsx. Call sites (src/frontend/src/tabs/admin.tsx) render <ConnectorGlyph connector=…/>; no component branches on a connector id to draw its own artwork. Guarded by src/frontend/src/components/ConnectorGlyph.test.tsx (renders the six, plus a scan of the whole src/ tree for the retired brand hexes, the retired path geometry, the retired component symbols and the retired asset filenames) and by the rewritten ConnectorLogos.test.tsx; ui-consistency-check.mjs no longer exempts ConnectorLogos.tsx from the hardcoded-colour lint.
connector-vendor-marks.obligation: none — no vendor mark or brand artwork is redistributed any more; the vendor NAMES remain as nominative textual references to supported interoperability
connector-vendor-marks.owner_decision: DECIDED 2026-09-05 (owner, tracker 239) — option (b): REPLACE the six marks with Correlix-owned generic functional glyphs, matching licence decision D5 for the cloud marks. Not 'record each vendor's terms': remove the question. Official third-party marks may only be added back by an explicit review with the usage terms recorded here first (docs/design/UI_CONNECTOR_MARKS.md).
connector-vendor-marks.posture: RESOLVED by replacement. Official connector marks are removed from the product UI. A third-party connector is now identified by a GENERIC FUNCTIONAL glyph from the product's own icon set plus the vendor's name as plain factual text — ServiceNow/ITSM ticket, Jira/work-item board, Slack/chat bubble, Microsoft Teams/collaborators, Twilio/handset, PagerDuty/incident beacon, unknown/integration plug. No vendor path data, brand colour or gradient remains anywhere in the tree, and the connector chips are styled from theme tokens instead of brand tints so they read correctly in light and dark.
connector-vendor-marks.rationale: The six were verbatim brand path data in brand colours, bundled into the shipped SPA with no usage terms recorded for any of them — the same class of exposure as the cloud marks D5 resolved, and invisible to the 2026-09-03 audit because the sweep closed the unreferenced asset files while the identical marks lived on inline WITH references. Recording six sets of brand terms would have left the default wrong: the next connector added would reach for the next official logo. Replacing them fixes the default instead, and costs nothing a customer values — the tiles still say ServiceNow, Jira, Slack, Twilio, PagerDuty and Microsoft Teams in plain text, which is the identification that actually does the work.

elkjs.evidence: EPL-2.0 text + EPL §3.2 source pointer ship as src/frontend/public/licenses/elkjs/LICENSE-EPL-2.0.txt and elkjs/SOURCE.txt; src/frontend/public/licenses/ (generated by src/frontend/scripts/gen-licenses.mjs, copied into dist/ by Vite and served at /licenses/ by the frontend image; Dockerfile.frontend also bakes docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md into /usr/share/nginx/html/licenses/)
elkjs.obligation: licence text + written source offer (upstream URL) in the shipped notices
elkjs.owner_decision: none needed — permissive-compatible for our use
elkjs.posture: BUNDLED VERBATIM into the SPA (dist/assets/elk.bundled-*.js). EPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft: we do not modify elkjs, so no source-disclosure of OUR code is triggered. EPL-2.0 §3.2 DOES require that recipients of the Object Code be told the licence and how to obtain Source. Vite strips the banner, so the notice MUST be carried by THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md shipped with the frontend image.

gotenberg/gotenberg.evidence: scripts/make-installer.sh licensing guards hard-fail the build if a gotenberg image appears in the base image set or in any add-on pack (alongside the existing redpanda/redis/prometheus guards); `pdf` is absent from BASE_PROFILES and from ADDONS.
gotenberg/gotenberg.owner_decision: DECIDED 2026-09-04 (owner) — the `pdf` profile NEVER enters a customer bundle. Adopting the audit's proposed rule as a mechanical build guard rather than a convention.
gotenberg/gotenberg.posture: Gotenberg's own code is MIT, but the image bundles PDFtk (GPL-2.0-or-later), LibreOffice (MPL-2.0), ttf-mscorefonts-installer (PROPRIETARY Microsoft EULA restricting redistribution) and, on amd64, Google Chrome (proprietary). It is NOT in any bundle today (the `pdf` profile is excluded from BASE_PROFILES), so no obligation is currently carried.
gotenberg/gotenberg.rationale: Gotenberg's own code is MIT, but the image bundles PDFtk (GPL-2.0-or-later), LibreOffice (MPL-2.0), ttf-mscorefonts-installer (a proprietary Microsoft EULA that restricts redistribution) and, on amd64, Google Chrome (proprietary, not Chromium). It is also pinned to a floating `:8` major tag, so its bundled-component licences can change between rebuilds without any change on our side. A convention that it 'must not ship' is worth nothing the day someone adds `--profile pdf` to BASE_PROFILES; a build failure is worth something.

grafana/grafana.evidence: Optional + separate: deployment/docker/docker-compose.yml service `grafana` is `profiles: ["self-monitoring"]` and `self-monitoring` is NOT in make-installer.sh BASE_PROFILES — it is cut as its own `correlix-addon-self-monitoring-<ver>.tar.zst` pack. Unmodified image: `grafana/grafana:11.2.0@sha256:408afb97...`, and no Dockerfile in the tree has a FROM on grafana (no patched image exists). Unmodified UI: the nginx /grafana/ route's `sub_filter` CSS injection — which repainted Grafana and HID its logo — was REMOVED on 2026-09-04 from deployment/docker/nginx/default.conf and default-mtls.conf; both now carry a do-not-reintroduce comment. Visual alignment is now GF_USERS_DEFAULT_THEME + kiosk mode, i.e. Grafana's own configuration. Notices: the `Grafana (AGPL-3.0) — optional self-monitoring add-on pack` licence text and the written source offer in docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md.
grafana/grafana.obligation: ship the AGPL-3.0 text + a written offer for Grafana's Corresponding Source (upstream URL); state prominently that Grafana is unmodified
grafana/grafana.owner_decision: DECIDED 2026-09-04 (owner) — KEEP. Grafana ships only in the optional `self-monitoring` add-on pack, as the unmodified upstream container, on its own route. Option (a) of audit D1. The add-on pack is a separate image archive the customer must explicitly enable; the base appliance does not contain it.
grafana/grafana.posture: Ships ONLY in the optional `self-monitoring` add-on pack, as an unmodified upstream container, reached on its own port/route. No Correlix code links to, embeds, or derives from Grafana; we do not modify it, so AGPL §13 imposes no obligation to offer OUR source.
grafana/grafana.rationale: AGPL-3.0 §13 binds the operator of a MODIFIED version to offer that version's source to its network users. Correlix neither modifies Grafana nor links to, embeds or derives from it: it is a stock digest-pinned image, configured only through Grafana's own GF_* environment variables and its provisioning directory (read-only mounts). Nothing in Correlix's source is therefore touched by the AGPL. What IS owed — the AGPL-3.0 text and an offer of Grafana's Corresponding Source — ships in the notices. The posture holds only while Grafana stays unmodified, which is now enforced rather than assumed (see `evidence`).

nms-vendor-theming.evidence: REMOVED: src/frontend/src/components/NmsVendorArt.tsx in its entirety — the NMS_THEMES per-vendor palette table, the MONOGRAM initials table, the gradient monogram chip and the per-vendor ART_TITLE window captions. NEW: src/frontend/src/components/NmsControllerArt.tsx — the controller → display name / functional category / Icon.tsx glyph / functional scene registry, with ONE theme-token palette shared by every controller and functional scene titles; plus the new `wireless` glyph in components/Icon.tsx. NEW: the `.nms-mark` chip in src/frontend/src/styles.css, derived from var(--accent)/var(--surface)/var(--panel-border) with no colour literal. Call sites (src/frontend/src/pages/NmsIntegrations.tsx) render <NmsMark vendor=…/> and <NmsDashArt vendor=…/>; no component branches on a controller id to draw its own artwork and the page contains no <svg> at all. Guarded by src/frontend/src/components/NmsControllerArt.test.tsx (45 assertions: registry mapping, functional-category and scene-title checks that fail if either names a product, byte-identity of every mark with the shared Icon.tsx glyph, no vendor hex / monogram / gradient / <text> in any rendered mark, no raw colour outside a var() token in any rendered scene, and a scan of the whole src/ tree for the retired palette hexes, the retired symbols, the retired monograms and the imitated console titles — including an assertion that NmsVendorArt.tsx no longer exists).
nms-vendor-theming.obligation: none — no vendor palette, monogram or console-chrome imitation is redistributed any more; the controller PRODUCT NAMES remain as nominative textual references to supported interoperability
nms-vendor-theming.owner_decision: DECIDED 2026-09-05 (owner, tracker 251) — REPLACE the vendor-coloured, vendor-shaped monograms with generic Correlix glyphs, matching the tracker 239 connector decision and licence decision D5 for the cloud marks. Vendor names may remain as factual text labels; no official or logo-like geometry; vendor-specific colours must not be preserved as pseudo-branding; reuse the existing generic-glyph framework.
nms-vendor-theming.posture: RESOLVED by replacement. The NMS connector gallery no longer carries any vendor palette. A controller is now identified by a GENERIC FUNCTIONAL glyph from the product's own icon set plus its product name as plain factual text — Meraki/wireless controller, Catalyst Center/campus assurance, SD-WAN Manager and Versa Director/SD-WAN and secure-edge, Nexus Dashboard/fabric controller, Versa Concerto/multi-tenant orchestration, Prime Infrastructure/NMS, unknown/integration plug. The dashboard-preview art survives but is keyed by FUNCTIONAL SCENE rather than by vendor and drawn entirely from theme tokens, so it is legible in light and dark and carries no brand hue.
nms-vendor-theming.rationale: The monogram chips were not a trademark reproduction — the file said so — but they were the one place left in the product where a third-party BRAND COLOUR carried identity: Meraki's green, Cisco's #049fd9, the Versa violets and the Prime greys, applied as a gradient behind a stylised two-letter initial, with the preview scene themed to match under a window caption that imitated the vendor's own console down to its hostname. A recoloured lookalike is still the mark and brand colour used as identity is pseudo-branding, both of which docs/design/UI_CONNECTOR_MARKS.md §4 already forbids; leaving this one exception in place would have left the DEFAULT wrong, so the next controller added would reach for the next vendor palette. Replacing it fixes the default and costs nothing a customer values — the tiles still say Meraki, Catalyst Center, SD-WAN Manager, Nexus Dashboard, Versa Director, Versa Concerto and Prime Infrastructure in plain text, which is the identification that actually does the work.

quay.io/keycloak/keycloak.evidence: The `Red Hat Universal Base Image EULA — Keycloak (sso profile)` licence text in docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md carries the terms URL and the acceptance statement; the image is a digest-pinned upstream reference in deployment/docker/docker-compose.yml with no Dockerfile FROM anywhere in the tree, so nothing of ours is layered onto it. Also recorded in docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md and the docs-portal deploy page.
quay.io/keycloak/keycloak.obligation: accept the Red Hat UBI EULA (https://www.redhat.com/licenses/EULA_Red_Hat_Universal_Base_Image_English_20190422.pdf), state the acceptance and the terms URL in the shipped notices, and redistribute the UBI-based image unmodified
quay.io/keycloak/keycloak.owner_decision: DECIDED 2026-09-04 (owner) — ACCEPT the Red Hat Universal Base Image End User Licence Agreement and document it in the ship set. Keycloak stays on its upstream UBI-based image; it is NOT rebased onto a non-UBI base.
quay.io/keycloak/keycloak.posture: Keycloak itself is Apache-2.0, but its base is Red Hat ubi9-micro, governed by the Red Hat Universal Base Image EULA rather than an OSS licence. The `sso` profile IS in BASE_PROFILES, so this image ships in the core bundle.
quay.io/keycloak/keycloak.rationale: The UBI EULA permits redistribution of the unmodified UBI image and of applications built on it, without a Red Hat subscription, provided the image is not modified in ways the EULA forbids and Red Hat's marks are not used to imply support. Correlix ships `quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:25.0` exactly as published — no rebuild, no FROM, no layer of ours on top — so the acceptance is a documentation duty, not an engineering one. Keycloak's own code remains Apache-2.0. Rebasing onto a non-UBI image would mean maintaining our own Keycloak build, which is a larger and riskier surface than accepting a redistribution-permitting EULA.

ietf-rfc-mibs.note: MIB modules reproduced from IETF RFCs are Code Components; the IETF Trust Legal Provisions license them under the Simplified/Modified BSD terms set out in section 4.e, so redistribution is permitted with the notice. Each file carries an ASCII header naming its RFC, the rfc-editor.org URL, the 'Code Component' status, the IETF Trust licence pointer (https://trustee.ietf.org/license-info) and the Internet Society copyright line. P-BRIDGE-MIB and Q-BRIDGE-MIB carry the Internet Society (2006) / RFC 4363 notice inline in the module text. SNMPv2-TC (RFC 2579, STD 58) and SNMPv2-CONF (RFC 2580, STD 58) joined this entry on 2026-09-04 under decision D3, replacing Cisco's edited extracts of the obsoleted RFC 1903/1904; the replacements were verified line-for-line against net-snmp's own upstream IETF copies.
